choices.text: Nothing: the heart is supposed to use up blood
Blood is not used up - it loops back to the heart and goes round again

questions.explanation: The trap is: The heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood. Scene s4 shows why this is wrong: Blood is never used up: it keeps going round in a loop, coming back to the heart to be pushed around again.
questions.misconception: The heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood.
questions.prompt: A pupil says: the heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood. What is wrong with this idea?

questions.explanation: Scene s1: chewed food travels from the mouth down to the stomach, where it is mixed, then on into the intestines, where the body takes out the good parts.
questions.prompt: In which order does food travel through the digestive system?

questions.answer: The lungs fill with air and grow bigger, then shrink as the air flows back out.
questions.explanation: Scene s2: air travels down the windpipe into the lungs, the lungs fill and grow bigger, then they shrink as air flows back out.
questions.prompt: What happens to the lungs when you breathe in, and what happens when you breathe out?

questions.answer: It travels back to the heart and goes round the loop again.
questions.explanation: Scene s3: the heart pumps blood out to the body, and the same blood travels back to the heart, keeping going round in a loop.
questions.prompt: A drop of blood leaves the heart and travels to the body. What happens to that drop next?

questions.explanation: Scene s2: air moves in and out of the lungs through the windpipe; the stomach and intestines belong to the digestive system in scene s1.
questions.prompt: Which organ fills with air when you breathe in?
